claims.text: The driver's own trace establishes the deviation. Between the recorded pickup and dropoff the polyline runs 17.08 km against a booked optimal of 13.9 km, an excess of 3.18 km — 22.88% of optimal, which clears the 20% gate, and well above the 0.8 km absolute gate. Both POL-RD-01 tests therefore pass and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The 17.1 km figure on the trip record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km (17.08 km) govern for the threshold test and expressly forbids citing the trip-record copy for it; the excess is measured on the trace, as it is here.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace and needs no independent corroboration.

The driver's stated cause — a bus breakdown that forced him via Balestier — fails for want of the very artifact POL-RD-03 requires. EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is MISSING: it carries weight 0.0 and fired issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, recording that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. I disclose that impairment rather than present the artifact as clean. POL-RD-03 exonerates only on a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses within an overlapping validity window; with no advisory there is nothing to run, and the driver's account is unsupported assertion. The absence is itself citable and defeats the excuse.

Once the rider has shown the threshold excess the burden is the driver's, and POL-RD-08 is explicit that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge it. No advisory ID, no closure record and no admission of an unjustified detour appears anywhere in this record, so nothing rebuts the established deviation.

No rider-requested detour can be made out: the trip's chat log carries zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so the POL-RD-04 instruction test and its corroboration test cannot be run and that clause exonerates no part of the excess.

No endpoint amendment supports a re-baseline: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-05 therefore cannot be run, and the booked optimal of 13.9 km stands as the baseline for the threshold test.

This is not a pooled trip. The vehicle type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application and no part of the excess can be attributed to collecting a co-rider; the booked single-rider optimal governs.

The rider owes no corroboration beyond the trace. POL-RD-08's rider-history factor engages only where deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more, and the rider's is 0 with 0 substantiated; the factor does not apply, and the trace alone proves the excess.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, the fare model being METERED. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 20.385 + 0.80 = 21.185. The surge multiplier is read from the fare_breakdown, where it is 1.0, and nowhere else. Refund = 26.95 - 21.185 = 5.765, rounded up to SGD 5.80 payable. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 21.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the upfront-quote rule has no purchase on this trip and the POL-RD-02 recomputation governs the remedy.

The driver's second point — that a taxi meter is dearer than the app's discount cars — is not a defence under any clause. POL-RD-01 measures the excess against the platform's optimal route for the booked product (13.9 km), not against the price of a different product tier; the vehicle's tier does not widen the corridor the driver is entitled to drive.

The rider does not claim the POL-RD-06 uplift, and on this record it is not available: the deviation at 22.9% is below the 50% MATERIAL gate and the driver's 90-day counters — 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips — show no pattern, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a conduct referral arises. The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial, and the rider rests on this trip's own trace rather than on the driver's history.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, and the case should be ruled rather than held. The trip identifiers on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all match TRP-00530; the pickup and dropoff timestamps are consistent across them; the trace has no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval above 30 seconds; and the artifacts carrying the deciding fact each weigh 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor. The rider's claim rests on the trace and the trip record, both complete; the driver's missing advisory defeats his excuse rather than leaving the rider's claim unprovable.

claims.text: Measured as the policy requires — the governing figure is the trace, gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 17.08 km against the booked optimal of 13.9 km — the excess is 3.18 km, or 22.88%. That clears POL-RD-01's two establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%), but it is nowhere near the materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50%, so this is at most an ordinary threshold-level deviation and not a MATERIAL one; the materiality-triggered machinery of POL-RD-01 does not engage.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to convert a modest excess into a full refund. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the clause's threshold of 3, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0, far below the 0.05 ratio and with well over the 40 trips the test requires. POL-RD-06's pattern consequences — in particular the FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral — therefore do not arise, and the profile cannot be used to build a pattern finding against the driver.

The driver's account is that a bus breakdown blocked the main road, so he took Balestier. But this record contains no advisory at all: EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is MISSING, flagged MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING) and carrying weight 0.0 — it can prove no fact, and its absence is itself citable. Without a traffic_advisory the POL-RD-03 test cannot be run, and POL-RD-10(5) makes a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory a mandatory escalation trigger. The correct disposition on this record is therefore ESCALATE: the disputed amount is HELD rather than refunded while a human reviews it.

The rider's narrative is habit and a fare comparison, not a distance measurement: it says the trip usually costs 'around fifty dollars' and that this taxi came to 'seventy-six', yet the ledger records SGD 26.95 charged for this very trip. The rider's own figures do not correspond to the record, and an allegation of a repeated pattern — 'how many times did I NOT check?' — that identifies no other trip and cites no other artifact carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the only measure of deviation the policy recognises is the distance derived from this trip's own trace.

The rider contests the entire SGD 26.95, but POL-RD-02 is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it caps any recovery. On the metered fare the recomputed figure is 21.1850 (base 3.80 plus 0.75 x 13.9 km plus 0.28 x 22 min = 20.385, at a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee), so the refund before rounding is 5.765 against a charged total of 26.95 — a refund share of 21.4%, far below the 90% FULL_REFUND threshold and with reaches_full_refund_share recorded as false. The rider's demand for the whole fare cannot be met on any view of this policy.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver — this trip's measurements are clear, but the record cannot test the driver's excuse, so a human reviewer must decide it; the disputed SGD 26.95 is HELD rather than collected or refunded.

The deviation is established. The governing figure is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00530): 17.08 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against the booked optimal of 13.9 km (EV-TRIP-00530), an excess of 3.18 km — 22.88% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (0.8 km and 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED; it is below the material gates (8.0 km / 50%), so POL-RD-01's material machinery and POL-RD-06's pattern check never engage — the driver's 90-day counters are 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips, no pattern, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral arise. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07 (205 fixes at 10 s cadence, no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, max gap 0 s), so the excess needs no independent corroboration. Nothing exonerates any part of it: the chat log is empty so POL-RD-04 cannot run, no endpoint was amended so POL-RD-05 cannot run, and this is RYDE_TAXI, not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. POL-RD-11 has no purchase (fare model METERED, quoted fare null).

On the merits the arithmetic would give the rider a partial refund, and I record the figure so the reviewer has it: under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.0 (surge read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 21.185, and the refund is 26.95 - 21.185 = 5.765, i.e. SGD 5.80, which is 21.4% of the charge — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share.

Why the case escalates. The driver's account is that a bus breakdown forced him via Balestier. That is an exculpatory claim under POL-RD-03, which requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, in a validity window overlapping the trip, matched by the vehicle leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor. No such advisory exists here: EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING), recording that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. POL-RD-10(5) makes a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory a mandatory escalation, so the driver's excuse can neither be accepted nor rejected on this record — a human must obtain the advisory records for that corridor and window (or establish that none was issued) before POL-RD-03 can be run. The driver's other point, that a metered taxi costs more than the app's discount cars, is not a defence: POL-RD-01 measures the excess against the platform's optimal route for the booked product, not against another product tier. I do not accept the rider's contention that no POL-RD-10 trigger fires — the absent advisory is exactly the (5) case. Because the only artifact bearing on that trigger, EV-ADVIS-00530-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0, my confidence is capped at 0.0 under POL-GEN-02(2); that is itself below the policy's 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) is engaged as well. The finding that the deviation is established is unaffected by that cap.

What the reviewer should do: confirm whether any traffic advisory covered the optimal corridor during 08:06-08:41 on 18 Sep 2026. If one exists, run POL-RD-03 (removing any justified excess) and recompute under POL-RD-02; if none exists, the deviation stands as established and the merits figure is the SGD 5.80 partial refund to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
This is a metered taxi trip (TRP-00530, RYDE_TAXI) from Hougang to Raffles Place. I cannot issue a final money ruling on this record. The SGD 26.95 is held — not refunded to the rider and not retained by the driver — pending human review.

What is established, for both parties. Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires — on gps_trace.trace_distance_km (17.08 km), and not on the trip record's rounded 17.1 km copy, which the clause forbids citing for the threshold test — the distance driven exceeded the booked optimal of 13.9 km by 3.18 km, or 22.88%. That passes both establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not reach the materiality gates (8.0 km or 50%), so the POL-RD-06 materiality machinery is not engaged. The trace is clean — 205 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0 — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and needs no independent corroboration. The driver's 90-day counters (0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips) show no repeat pattern, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises.

Why the case cannot be finally ruled. The driver's account is that a bus breakdown on the main road forced the Balestier route. That is an assertion of an external traffic event, and only POL-RD-03 can excuse it — but POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, within the trip window. There is none. EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the BLOCKING issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. Its absence is citable, but the consequence is that the driver's excuse can neither be confirmed nor dismissed on this record. I do not accept the rider's submission that this absence merely 'defeats his excuse' and leaves the case decidable: where an exculpatory clause is invoked and the artifact it depends on is missing from the pool — the policy's own example is 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' — POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory. No monetary outcome therefore issues and the disputed amount is held.

What would resolve it. A traffic_advisory valid for 18 September 2026, covering approximately 08:06–08:41 SGT, naming a road or segment on the optimal Hougang–Raffles Place corridor, together with the shortest lawful alternative distance if a closure is claimed, would let POL-RD-03 be run and this case be decided on its merits.

Claim points that do not change the outcome. The driver's second point — that a taxi meter is dearer than the app's discount cars — is not a defence under any clause: POL-RD-01 measures the excess against the platform's optimal route for the booked product, not against the price of a different product tier. No rider-requested detour applies (the chat log has zero messages and no waypoint_hint, POL-RD-04); no endpoint was amended (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, POL-RD-05); and this is not a pooled trip (RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, POL-RD-12). The fare model is METERED with a null quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 has no purchase. There are no ERP or surcharge lines in the fare breakdown to correct under POL-RD-09 (erp total 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00), and the rider's history factor under POL-RD-08 does not engage (deviation_claims_60d 0). The rider's narrative of 'around fifty' versus 'seventy-six' is a fare comparison, not a distance measurement, and does not correspond to the SGD 26.95 charged on this trip.

For the reviewer's information only (not ordered today): had the case been decidable, POL-RD-02 on this METERED fare would give recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 13.9 + 0.28 × 22.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 = 21.185, so a refund of 26.95 − 21.185 = 5.765, rounded UP to SGD 5.80 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 21.4% of charged_total, i.e. a PARTIAL_REFUND. The surge multiplier of 1.0 was read from the fare_breakdown, where the policy places it.

Confidence 0.70: the deviation finding is carried by weight-1.0 artifacts (the GPS trace and the trip record), but the exculpatory limb turns on an artifact that is absent, so the merits cannot be resolved on this record.

Both of you are right about the measurement, and the measurement is right. The governing figure is the trace, not the trip record's rounded copy: the GPS polyline for TRP-00530 runs 17.08 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against the booked optimal of 13.9 km — an excess of 3.18 km, or 22.88% of optimal. That clears both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%), so the deviation is established; it clears neither materiality gate (8.0 km, 50%), so POL-RD-06's machinery never engages, and in any event the driver's 90-day record (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips) shows no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral. Nothing else excuses the excess: the chat log carries no messages, so no rider-requested detour arises under POL-RD-04; no pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the vehicle is RYDE_TAXI rather than RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 is irrelevant; and the fare is METERED with no upfront quote, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 205 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, no sustained sampling above 30 seconds — so POL-RD-07 does not bite and no independent corroboration is required. The rider's pay records are not in evidence, so the driver's remark that a taxi meter is dearer than the app's discount-car tier is not a defence under any clause and I put it aside. The deviation finding rests on EV-GPS-00530 and EV-TRIP-00530, each at weight 1.0, so it is not discounted.

The reason I do not rule on the money is the driver's explanation for the diversion. He says a bus breakdown forced him through Balestier. That is a closure-type explanation, and the artifact that would test it is absent: EV-ADVIS-00530-01 carries weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) — no traffic advisory covers the optimal corridor in this trip's window. POL-RD-03 exonerates only on an advisory naming a road the optimal route uses within an overlapping validity window; the advisory is missing, so the clause cannot be run, and the driver's account does not stand in for it, because POL-RD-03's test reads an advisory, not a statement. POL-RD-08 makes the same point from the burden side — a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic-advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's shifted burden — so the deviation stands established. But POL-RD-10(5) is engaged where an exculpatory clause is invoked against an artifact that is missing from the pool or does not cover the trip window, and it gives 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' as its own example: that is exactly this record. The case must therefore go to a human reviewer. Escalation is terminal — no money moves, and the disputed SGD 26.95 is held rather than collected or refunded.

What would resolve it: the LTA advisory record, or a bus-operator incident report, for the optimal corridor between roughly 08:06 and 08:40 on 18 September 2026. If no incident is confirmed, the arithmetic both sides have set out applies — recomputed fare (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 21.185, refund 26.95 - 21.185 = 5.765, rounded up to SGD 5.80, a PARTIAL_REFUND.

Two of the rider's arguments I do not accept, though neither changes the outcome. First, the rider says no POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case should be ruled rather than held; that submission works through the identifier, timestamp, trace-integrity and confidence triggers but says nothing about the missing-advisory trigger, which is the one that fires. Second, the rider's narrative — a usual fare of 'around fifty dollars' against 'seventy-six' for this trip — does not correspond to the ledger, which records SGD 26.95 charged on this very trip, and the claim of a repeated pattern identifies no other trip and cites no other artifact; those assertions carry no weight. That does not matter, because the deviation is proved by this trip's trace rather than by either party's account.

No referral arises on these facts: the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(4) produces nothing, and there is no repeat-deviation finding to refer under POL-RD-06(c). The only open question is the one named above, and it belongs here in the explanation, not in the referrals list.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case cannot be decided in money, and I am sending it to a human reviewer under POL-RD-10(5). Here is why, and what I found on the way.

The deviation itself is real and is established. Measured as POL-RD-01 requires — on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the trip record's rounded convenience copy of 17.1 km — the drive was 17.08 km against the booked optimal route of 13.9 km. The excess is 3.18 km, or 22.9% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the rider's core measurement is accepted. It does not reach either materiality gate (8.0 km or 50%), so no POL-RD-06 pattern machinery is engaged.

What stops a money ruling is the driver's explanation. He says a bus breakdown blocked the main road and forced him via Balestier. That is a road-closure excuse, and this policy can only accept or reject it against a traffic_advisory. There is no advisory on this record: EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is a missing artifact — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING). Under POL-GEN-02(3) I name it: it is at weight 0.0 and can carry no fact, and its absence is itself citable. POL-RD-10(5) makes 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' a mandatory escalation, and it is not answered by POL-RD-08's burden rule — POL-RD-08 decides whose assertion fails, it does not decide whether a human should look at a closure claim the platform's own advisory data cannot confirm. ESCALATE is terminal: the disputed SGD 26.95 is held, not collected and not refunded.

So nothing is lost, I record the arithmetic both of you argued over. Had the matter been ruled on the deviation, POL-RD-02 (the fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply) would have given: charged_total 26.95; recomputed_fare 21.185 = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 13.9 km + 0.28 x 22 min = 20.385) x the fare_breakdown surge multiplier of 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee; refund 5.765, rounded up to SGD 5.80 payable. That is 21.4% of the charge — a PARTIAL_REFUND, not the full SGD 26.95 the rider seeks. The rider's demand for the whole fare is rejected on that arithmetic, and the driver's tier argument ('a taxi meter is dearer than the discount app cars') is no defence under any clause: the corridor the driver may drive is the platform's optimal route for the booked product, not another product's price. The rider's 'around fifty dollars / seventy-six dollars' narrative names no other trip and cites no other artifact, so it carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the only deviation measure is this trip's own trace. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral and no POL-RD-02 full-refund uplift arise: 22.9% is below the materiality gate and the driver's trailing 90-day counters (0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips) show no pattern.

Confidence is 0.5, below the 0.70 platform floor. The disposition turns on an artifact that is absent at weight 0.0, and the only support for the driver's closure account is an unweighted counterparty statement; the deviation evidence itself is clean at weight 1.0, but it is not what decides this outcome.

What would resolve this for the reviewer: a traffic_advisory naming a road on the optimal corridor with a validity window overlapping this trip, or a platform record or driver admission establishing whether the road was in fact blocked. With that, the case can be decided on POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-02.

ledger.claim: The driver's own trace establishes the deviation. Between the recorded pickup and dropoff the polyline runs 17.08 km against a booked optimal of 13.9 km, an excess of 3.18 km — 22.88% of optimal, which clears the 20% gate, and well above the 0.8 km absolute gate. Both POL-RD-01 tests therefore pass and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The 17.1 km figure on the trip record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km (17.08 km) govern for the threshold test and expressly forbids citing the trip-record copy for it; the excess is measured on the trace, as it is here.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace and needs no independent corroboration.

The driver's stated cause — a bus breakdown that forced him via Balestier — fails for want of the very artifact POL-RD-03 requires. EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is MISSING: it carries weight 0.0 and fired issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, recording that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. I disclose that impairment rather than present the artifact as clean. POL-RD-03 exonerates only on a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses within an overlapping validity window; with no advisory there is nothing to run, and the driver's account is unsupported assertion. The absence is itself citable and defeats the excuse.

ledger.claim: No rider-requested detour can be made out: the trip's chat log carries zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so the POL-RD-04 instruction test and its corroboration test cannot be run and that clause exonerates no part of the excess.

No endpoint amendment supports a re-baseline: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-05 therefore cannot be run, and the booked optimal of 13.9 km stands as the baseline for the threshold test.

This is not a pooled trip. The vehicle type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application and no part of the excess can be attributed to collecting a co-rider; the booked single-rider optimal governs.

The rider owes no corroboration beyond the trace. POL-RD-08's rider-history factor engages only where deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more, and the rider's is 0 with 0 substantiated; the factor does not apply, and the trace alone proves the excess.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, the fare model being METERED. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.9 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 20.385 + 0.80 = 21.185. The surge multiplier is read from the fare_breakdown, where it is 1.0, and nowhere else. Refund = 26.95 - 21.185 = 5.765, rounded up to SGD 5.80 payable. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 21.4% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the upfront-quote rule has no purchase on this trip and the POL-RD-02 recomputation governs the remedy.

The driver's second point — that a taxi meter is dearer than the app's discount cars — is not a defence under any clause. POL-RD-01 measures the excess against the platform's optimal route for the booked product (13.9 km), not against the price of a different product tier; the vehicle's tier does not widen the corridor the driver is entitled to drive.

The rider does not claim the POL-RD-06 uplift, and on this record it is not available: the deviation at 22.9% is below the 50% MATERIAL gate and the driver's 90-day counters — 0 deviation flags over 250 completed trips — show no pattern, so neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor a conduct referral arises. The rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial, and the rider rests on this trip's own trace rather than on the driver's history.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, and the case should be ruled rather than held. The trip identifiers on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all match TRP-00530; the pickup and dropoff timestamps are consistent across them; the trace has no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m and no sampling interval above 30 seconds; and the artifacts carrying the deciding fact each weigh 1.0, so confidence is not capped below the 0.70 floor. The rider's claim rests on the trace and the trip record, both complete; the driver's missing advisory defeats his excuse rather than leaving the rider's claim unprovable.

Measured as the policy requires — the governing figure is the trace, gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 17.08 km against the booked optimal of 13.9 km — the excess is 3.18 km, or 22.88%. That clears POL-RD-01's two establishment gates (0.8 km and 20%), but it is nowhere near the materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50%, so this is at most an ordinary threshold-level deviation and not a MATERIAL one; the materiality-triggered machinery of POL-RD-01 does not engage.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to convert a modest excess into a full refund. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the clause's threshold of 3, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0, far below the 0.05 ratio and with well over the 40 trips the test requires. POL-RD-06's pattern consequences — in particular the FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral — therefore do not arise, and the profile cannot be used to build a pattern finding against the driver.

The driver's account is that a bus breakdown blocked the main road, so he took Balestier. But this record contains no advisory at all: EV-ADVIS-00530-01 is MISSING, flagged MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING) and carrying weight 0.0 — it can prove no fact, and its absence is itself citable. Without a traffic_advisory the POL-RD-03 test cannot be run, and POL-RD-10(5) makes a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory a mandatory escalation trigger. The correct disposition on this record is therefore ESCALATE: the disputed amount is HELD rather than refunded while a human reviews it.

The rider's narrative is habit and a fare comparison, not a distance measurement: it says the trip usually costs 'around fifty dollars' and that this taxi came to 'seventy-six', yet the ledger records SGD 26.95 charged for this very trip. The rider's own figures do not correspond to the record, and an allegation of a repeated pattern — 'how many times did I NOT check?' — that identifies no other trip and cites no other artifact carries no weight under POL-RD-08; the only measure of deviation the policy recognises is the distance derived from this trip's own trace.

The rider contests the entire SGD 26.95, but POL-RD-02 is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it caps any recovery. On the metered fare the recomputed figure is 21.1850 (base 3.80 plus 0.75 x 13.9 km plus 0.28 x 22 min = 20.385, at a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee), so the refund before rounding is 5.765 against a charged total of 26.95 — a refund share of 21.4%, far below the 90% FULL_REFUND threshold and with reaches_full_refund_share recorded as false. The rider's demand for the whole fare cannot be met on any view of this policy.
